core.fantasy: You are a tiny new cell in a drop of water, eating, growing and redesigning yourself until you are big enough to leave the pool.
pillars: Eat or be eaten, by size
Grow and the world rises with you
core.signature_moment: You fit a new spike from a fallen meteor fragment, swim back out, and the thing that chased you a minute ago is now your lunch.
anti_goals: no harsh failure: death respawns you from an egg

signatures.description: Who eats whom is decided by size and parts you can see: smaller things are food, bigger things are danger.
A mating call opens a playful editor where you drag parts (mouths, spikes, flagella, eyes, poison) onto your cell, paint it and swim off changed.
New parts are found in the world, in meteor fragments and in creatures you eat, then become editor choices.
The pool is stacked in parallax layers: blurred giants drift below, sunlit specks float above, and growing lifts you to the next layer.
The mouth you choose sets your diet (plants, meat or both), which changes how you play.

size_classes.prey: smaller than you: food, no threat
size_classes.peer: your size: a fair fight; beating one drops 3 meat chunks
size_classes.predator: bigger: kills you in two hits
size_classes.epic: giant: kills you in one hit; only clever play beats it

mechanics.growth: Five size stages, each split in two (ten steps). Each step needs about five pieces of food; every step turns your old peers into prey. Seeing the seafloor means you are nearly ready to leave the water.
food: small green plant bits and big seaweed (herbivore)
eggs later in the stage: anyone can eat them, left alone they hatch predators
living cells drained with a proboscis
world_objects: meteor fragments to ram open for parts
currents that speed you up with them and slow you against them

parts.spikes: only protect and hit where they point; long ones catch on terrain
parts.poison: leaves a cloud behind that slows and hurts chasers
parts.electric: charges up then zaps around you
parts.eyes: without eyes your view is restricted

mechanics.diet: Diet is a sliding timeline from herbivore to carnivore: you start in the middle, plants push one way, meat and kills the other, and later choices count less. The final diet sets a bonus that carries into the next stage.
editor_flow: press Call Mate (or the key) at any time
a mate appears and calls; follow the sound
the cell editor opens in a top-down view of your cell
drag parts on (placement matters: spikes cover only where they sit, a thin body is harder to hit), paint, sell parts back for DNA
leave: you hatch as the new design and swim on

input.controls: WASD or arrow keys, or click to set a destination; + and - zoom; one key pauses (camera and commands still work while paused).

rendering.signature: Cell Stage: soft translucent 3D cells with glowing rims, seen straight down, floating in parallax layers of water whose blur and tint grow with depth, so giant creatures drift past below like shadows.
rendering.lesson: A top-down 2D game can still have depth: stack the pool in blurred, tinted layers and move the player up a layer as they grow. Our film-look depth of field and an SVG or shader cell rim do the rest.

art.motion: procedural; Animators author motion once in a special editor on test creatures, marked up by meaning (this is a hand, this is a mouth)

body.note: Your cell picture and health sit in the bottom-right corner. When anything is hit, a small bar appears above it: green for health left, red for the last hit, black for what was lost before.

threat.note: Size is the threat readout: smaller is food, same size is a fair fight, bigger is a predator and giants are epics. The next size class drifts blurred in the layer below before you reach it.

goals.note: A progress bar along the bottom fills with DNA toward the next evolution; when it is full the bottom-right button becomes the advance button. Meteor fragments in the world hold new parts.

tools.note: The cell editor is a separate screen opened by a mating call; changes show at once on the cell.

navigation.note: No map: you drift where the food is; the edge of the drop is soft.

screen_budget.fade_rule: Only health and the DNA bar while you swim; the editor is summoned.
screen_budget.layout: Health portrait bottom right, progress bar along the bottom, Call Mate button; damage bars appear on whoever is hit, then fade.

information_grammar.note: The cell carries most of it: parts show what it can do, size shows who can eat whom, and bigger shapes drift by in blurred layers below. A thin DNA bar and health are the only overlay; the editor is summoned by a mating call.

music.genre: generative ambient (Brian Eno with the audio team)
music.note: Procedural music that keeps changing rather than looping one track.

tricks: Animators author motion once in a special editor on test creatures, marked up by meaning (this is a hand, this is a mouth)
At runtime the motion is retargeted to any creature the player built, with an IK solver placing feet, hands and mouths
Paint is procedural too: brush scripts read the body and flare colour at the ends of limbs
animation.lesson: Animate by meaning, not by bone: author "reach with the mouth" once and retarget it to any shape the child makes.

take.setting: Size decides who eats whom, shown on the creatures themselves; being eaten just pops you back out of an egg.
Parts found in the goo become choices in a playful cell editor; every change shows at once in how Abbie's cell swims.
A top-down drop of water drawn in SVG and shaders: soft translucent cells with glowing rims, and parallax layers that blur and tint with depth.
Growing lifts the camera to the next, bigger layer of the pool, where the old giants are now your size.

leave: its later stages (creature, tribe, civilisation, space)

study_notes.why: Evan asked for a video of the Cell Stage for Abbie's science adventure (AW-STUDY-0047).
study_notes.video: Cloud sessions cannot reach YouTube, so public video was studied through written guides. A private recording from Evan's own copy on his PC was requested; its notes replace these estimates when it lands. Frames and recordings are study only and are never committed or published.
findings_for_the_science_adventure: Movement is on one flat plane inside a 3D pool: a top-down 2D game with real depth behind it.
Ten small growth steps of about five foods each keep a reward every minute or so.
Prey, peer, predator, epic: four size classes are the whole threat grammar, readable at a glance.
Damage bars live on the creature that was hit, not in a corner.
The mate call makes editing a moment in the world (follow the sound), not a menu.
Parts work only where you put them, so the editor is a real decision, not decoration.
Eggs that hatch into predators if left: a gentle clock without a timer.
Currents and poison clouds make the water itself part of play.
